message.content:
当前基线的 GET /requests/{request_id}/evidence 已返回稳定的紧凑 JSON 证据快照，包含 request_id、status、event_count、chain_hash 和 verified，但只有 audit-bundle 支持条件读取。我要把这个 HTTP 入口扩展为可缓存读取：每次成功返回证据时都带强 ETag，格式为 "sha256:<64 个小写十六进制字符>"，摘要覆盖实际发送的完整响应体字节，包括末尾换行；相同证据在重复读取和进程重启后标签相同，状态、事件数或链摘要变化导致响应体变化时标签随之变化。

GET /requests/{request_id}/evidence 接受一个可选 If-None-Match 请求头，按 HTTP 实体标签列表解析。单个请求头中的强标签与当前 ETag 精确相同，或值为 * 时返回 304，响应体为空、Content-Length 为 0，并携带与完整响应相同的 ETag；标签不匹配、列表只有弱标签或弱标签与强标签混合时，仍返回现有 200 证据 JSON 和完整响应体。没有该请求头时也返回 200 和 ETag。多个 If-None-Match 请求头、空值、控制字符、未闭合引号、标签内部空格、尾随逗号或其他非法列表语法都返回 400 和 {"error":"invalid_request"}，并在读取请求存储前拒绝；合法请求仍按现有鉴权、租户解析、请求编号规范化和存储异常顺序得到 401、403、404、400、503。已有证据内容、字段顺序、紧凑 JSON、隐私字段屏蔽、跨租户不可见以及 verified=false 仍可正常读取的结果均不得改变。

本次只增加 evidence 路由的条件读取契约，不改变 audit-bundle 的 ETag 规则，也不改变其他 GET、POST、HEAD 或不支持方法的路由、状态码、Allow 头和错误 JSON。请补充公开 HTTP 回归覆盖，至少验证 ETag 与字节体对应、304 空体语义、弱标签不命中、证据变化后旧标签不命中、非法条件头先于存储访问被拒绝，以及原有成功和异常入口保持兼容。

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

1	"""HTTP layer for deletion-request acceptance, lookup, observation and
2	single-request and batched reconciliation.
3	
4	The service exposes fifteen business endpoints:
5	
6	* ``POST /requests`` -- accept a deletion request for a tenant. The JSON
7	  body must carry non-empty ``tenant_id``, ``subject_id`` and
8	  ``idempotency_key`` strings plus a non-empty ``scopes`` array of
9	  distinct non-empty strings.
10	* ``GET /requests`` -- the tenant-scoped, paginated listing of accepted
11	  requests. The tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule;
12	  the optional ``status`` (comma-separated distinct lifecycle statuses),
13	  ``created_from`` (inclusive) and ``created_to`` (exclusive) RFC3339 UTC
14	  bounds, ``cursor`` and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100) query
15	  parameters filter and page the result. The single-line JSON body
16	  carries exactly ``items`` and ``next_cursor``; each item carries
17	  exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` in ascending
18	  acceptance order, and ``next_cursor`` is the opaque continuation value
19	  or ``null`` at the end of the listing. Any other query parameter, a
20	  duplicated ``status`` value or a malformed filter answers 400.
21	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}`` -- return the accepted request's
22	  receipt, scoped to the tenant identified by the ``X-Tenant-Id`` header
23	  (or a ``tenant_id`` query parameter). The receipt is the record frozen
24	  at acceptance time and always reports ``accepted``; it never changes
25	  when the request's status subsequently advances.
26	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/status`` -- read-only observation of the
27	  request's current state. The single-line JSON body carries exactly
28	  ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` in that order; ``status``
29	  is the latest persisted state while ``created_at`` stays the original
30	  acceptance time.
31	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/execution-log`` -- read-only observation
32	  of the request's execution attempts. The single-line JSON body carries
33	  exactly ``request_id`` and ``attempts``; attempts are ordered by
34	  ``attempt_number`` starting at 1 and each entry carries exactly
35	  ``attempt_number``, ``claimed_at``, ``lease_expires_at``, ``result``
36	  and ``completed_at``. An unfinished attempt has ``null`` ``result`` and
37	  ``completed_at``; a finished attempt carries its stored ``completed``
38	  or ``failed`` result and completion time.
39	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/tombstones`` -- read-only, paginated
40	  publication of the tenant's deletion proofs for one request. The
41	  tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the only
42	  query parameters are ``cursor`` and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100).
43	  The single-line JSON body carries exactly ``request_id``,
44	  ``tombstones``, ``recorded_at``, ``evidence_digest`` and
45	  ``next_cursor`` in that order. ``tombstones`` holds only this page's
46	  entries in ascending normalized-scope Unicode code point order then
47	  ascending ``adapter_id``; each entry carries exactly ``adapter_id``,
48	  ``scope``, ``operation_id``, ``outcome`` (``deleted`` or ``absent``),
49	  ``proof_digest`` (64 lowercase hex characters) and ``recorded_at``.
50	  The top-level ``recorded_at`` and ``evidence_digest`` always describe
51	  the whole ledger (both ``null`` when it is empty), never just the
52	  page; ``next_cursor`` resumes strictly after this page's last entry
53	  while the ledger holds a following item and is ``null`` at the end.
54	  An unknown or duplicated query parameter, an invalid ``limit`` or an
55	  empty, malformed, foreign or stale ``cursor`` answers 400; an
56	  invalid, unknown or cross-tenant request id answers 404; a storage
57	  fault or a corrupt ledger answers 503 and never a partial page or a
58	  pseudo digest. The read never advances state, never creates an
59	  attempt or a tombstone and never changes the audit chain.
60	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/evidence`` -- read-only request-level
61	  integrity verdict. The tenant follows the existing
62	  ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule and the endpoint requires the
63	  ``request:read`` role. The single-line JSON body carries exactly
64	  ``request_id``, ``status``, ``event_count``, ``chain_hash`` and
65	  ``verified`` in that order: ``status`` and ``event_count`` are the
66	  current status and state-event count from the same database snapshot,
67	  ``chain_hash`` is that snapshot's persisted 64-character lowercase
68	  hexadecimal chain head (``null`` when the persisted value is not legal
69	  SHA-256 text), and ``verified`` is true only when the events are
70	  replayed event by event from that same snapshot -- every link
71	  recomputes to its stored hash from the genesis predecessor, sequences
72	  run gap-free from zero, the final event's status equals the current
73	  status and the final link equals the head bound to the request row.
74	  All five fields come from one committed snapshot, so a status advance
75	  or a concurrent write can never mix two transactions in one response.
76	  When the request row, events and head are readable, a deleted,
77	  altered, inserted, reordered or cross-request/cross-tenant rebound
78	  event -- or a head that is not legal SHA-256 text -- still answers 200
79	  with ``verified`` false (and a malformed head renders ``chain_hash``
80	  null); it is never a storage fault. A malformed, unknown or
81	  cross-tenant request id answers 404; a missing or invalid tenant
82	  answers 400; an unreadable database or a snapshot that cannot be read
83	  completely answers 503. The read never creates or changes a request,
84	  a state event, an execution attempt, a tombstone, a receipt, a policy
85	  catalog or an audit anchor.
86	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/audit-diagnosis`` -- read-only diagnosis
87	  of the request's persisted audit chain, the reason-carrying companion
88	  of the evidence verdict. The tenant follows the existing
89	  ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule and the endpoint requires the
90	  ``request:read`` role; the query string accepts no parameter other
91	  than ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated key, an unknown parameter or a
92	  missing or invalid tenant answers 400. The single-line JSON body
93	  carries exactly ``request_id``, ``trusted`` and ``reasons`` in that
94	  order: ``request_id`` is the normalized lowercase UUID, ``reasons``
95	  is the deduplicated list of stable, detail-free reason codes from
96	  :meth:`RequestStore.diagnose_chain` for the current database
97	  snapshot, sorted by Unicode code point, and ``trusted`` is true only
98	  when ``reasons`` is empty. An unanchored chain, a failed anchor
99	  authentication, an anchor head mismatch, a deleted, altered,
100	  inserted, reordered or cross-request/cross-tenant substituted event
101	  still answers 200 with non-empty ``reasons`` -- a diagnosable
102	  integrity problem is never a read failure. Repeated reads of the same
103	  persisted chain without new writes return byte-identical bodies, and
104	  no subject, raw scope, idempotency key, execution credential, anchor
105	  secret, SQL text or filesystem path is ever exposed. A malformed,
106	  unknown or cross-tenant request id answers 404; an unreadable
107	  database, an incomplete snapshot or a corrupt persisted record
108	  answers 503. The read never repairs, backfills, recomputes or
109	  overwrites anything: it never creates or changes a request, a state
110	  event, an execution attempt, a tombstone, a receipt, an audit anchor
111	  or a key generation, and it never writes an audit event or creates a
112	  batch.
113	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/audit-bundle`` -- read-only export of
114	  the request's settled audit chain as a portable evidence bundle. The
115	  tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule and the
116	  endpoint requires the ``request:read`` role; the query string accepts
117	  no parameter other than ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated key, an unknown
118	  parameter or a missing or conflicting tenant answers 400. The body is
119	  the verbatim single-line compact UTF-8 JSON text (with its single
120	  trailing newline) produced by
121	  :meth:`RequestStore.export_audit_bundle` from the same database
122	  snapshot -- never wrapped in a response object, re-ordered, indented
123	  or summarised. Repeated reads at the same chain head return
124	  byte-identical bodies; status events appended afterwards produce a
125	  new bundle but never change a previously rendered text, and no other
126	  request's events, a subject, a raw scope, an idempotency key, a claim
127	  credential or any anchor secret is ever exposed. A malformed, unknown
128	  or cross-tenant request id answers 404 with one detail-free outcome;
129	  a request whose audit chain has not settled, whose historical anchor
130	  secret is missing or whose evidence is untrusted answers 409 with
131	  exactly ``audit_bundle_unavailable`` and never a partial text; an
132	  unreadable database, a failed snapshot read or corrupt evidence
133	  answers 503. The read never modifies persisted evidence, never
134	  writes an audit event and never creates a batch.
135	  The export also honours HTTP conditional reads: every 200 response
136	  carries a strong ``ETag`` of the form ``"sha256:<64 lowercase hex>"``
137	  computed over the exact body bytes, so the same body always yields
138	  the same tag -- across repeat reads, concurrent readers and process
139	  restarts -- and any body change yields a different tag. A request
140	  may send one ``If-None-Match`` header holding a comma-separated list
141	  of entity tags; when any whitespace-stripped double-quoted tag is
142	  exactly equal to the current tag, or a tag is ``*`` and the bundle
143	  is exportable, the answer is ``304`` with no body, a zero
144	  ``Content-Length`` and the same ``ETag`` instead of the full 200
145	  body. Non-matching tags, lists where no tag matches and weak
146	  ``W/``-prefixed tags all receive the full 200 body. More than one
147	  ``If-None-Match`` header, an empty field value, a control character
148	  or a value that is neither a legal double-quoted entity tag nor
149	  ``*`` answers 400 with exactly ``invalid_request`` after
150	  authentication, tenant and query validation but before any storage
151	  access. The 404/409/503 outcomes above still take precedence over
152	  the conditional evaluation: the tag is only compared once the
153	  bundle has been exported, and the conditional read never writes to
154	  the database, generates an event or changes the exported bytes.
155	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/deletion-receipt`` -- read-only
156	  publication of the request's already-settled deletion execution
157	  receipt, so a caller recovers the frozen receipt without ever
158	  touching a signature key. The tenant follows the existing
159	  ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule and the endpoint requires the
160	  ``request:read`` role; the query string accepts no parameter other
161	  than ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated key, an unknown parameter or a
162	  missing or empty tenant answers 400. The body is the verbatim
163	  single-line compact UTF-8 JSON text (with its single trailing
164	  newline) returned by :meth:`RequestStore.get_receipt` for the same
165	  tenant and request -- exactly ``tenant_id``, ``request_id``,
166	  ``created_at``, ``completed_at``, ``scope_digest``,
167	  ``attempt_digest`` and ``tag`` in that fixed order, never wrapped,
168	  re-ordered, indented or recomputed. Repeated reads, reads across a
169	  process rebuild, concurrent reads and reads before and after a
170	  receipt key rotation all return byte-identical bodies, and no
171	  subject, raw scope, idempotency key, signature key, key fingerprint
172	  or execution credential is ever exposed. A malformed, unknown or
173	  cross-tenant request id answers 404 with one detail-free outcome; a
174	  request that exists but has no settled first receipt answers 409
175	  with exactly ``receipt_unavailable``; an unreadable database, a
176	  corrupt persisted receipt or an inconsistent snapshot answers 503.
177	  The read never mints a receipt, never registers a key generation,
178	  never advances any state and never rewrites any evidence.
179	* ``GET /policy-catalog/versions`` -- read-only publication of the
180	  tenant's policy-catalog version history, without any subject detail.
181	  The tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the query
182	  string accepts no parameter other than ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated
183	  key, an unknown parameter or an empty or malformed tenant answers 400.
184	  The body is the verbatim single-line compact UTF-8 JSON text (with its
185	  single trailing newline) produced by
186	  :meth:`RequestStore.audit_policy_catalog`: exactly ``versions`` at the
187	  top level, versions in ascending order, each carrying exactly
188	  ``version``, ``effective_at``, ``rule_count``, ``exception_count`` and
189	  ``status`` -- never a policy id, selector, reason, subject or any raw
190	  catalog content. The read never creates or advances a catalog version,
191	  request, attempt, tombstone, receipt or audit record, so repeated
192	  reads and reads after a restart return the same snapshot. A tenant
193	  without publications answers 200 with an empty ``versions`` array; a
194	  corrupt catalog or any storage failure answers 503 and never a
195	  partial history or a fabricated summary.
196	* ``POST /policy-catalog/versions`` -- the single policy-catalog
197	  publication entry point. The JSON body must carry exactly
198	  ``tenant_id``, ``rules`` and ``exceptions``: the tenant is taken from
199	  the body alone, and the two catalogs follow the existing retention
200	  format -- ``rules`` maps each policy id to exactly ``selector``,
201	  ``days`` and ``reason`` and must hold the whole-data ``*`` default
202	  rule, ``exceptions`` maps each policy id to the same three plus
203	  ``subject``, with policy ids unique across both catalogs. The catalogs
204	  are normalized with the existing selector grammar, non-boolean
205	  non-negative day counts and non-empty reasons before storage is
206	  touched. On success the single-line JSON body carries exactly
207	  ``version`` and ``effective_at``: the first publication is version 1,
208	  republishing the same normalized catalog reuses the first version and
209	  its effective time without writing, and a different catalog is issued
210	  the next consecutive version. Concurrent identical publications land
211	  once; concurrent publications of different catalogs have a single
212	  winner and every losing call answers 409 with exactly
213	  ``policy_catalog_conflict``. A non-object body, missing or extra
214	  fields, an illegal catalog shape, an out-of-range value, a missing
215	  default rule or a duplicated policy id answers 400 and writes nothing;
216	  a storage fault or a failed transaction answers 503 and never leaves
217	  a half-written version.
218	* ``POST /requests/{request_id}/reconcile`` -- reconcile exactly one
219	  request's execution record against its persisted state by calling the
220	  storage layer's :meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_execution`. The endpoint
221	  takes no business parameters: a missing ``Content-Length`` or a length
222	  of zero means there is no body; any other body answers 400. On success
223	  it answers 200 with the same single-line JSON shape as the status
224	  read -- exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` --
225	  rendering the current record after reconciliation. Repeating the call
226	  never changes a stable terminal state, historical attempts or existing
227	  timestamps; concurrent calls leave the unique outcome to the store's
228	  atomic commit. No subject, scope, idempotency key, worker, lease
229	  credential or attempt detail is ever exposed.
230	* ``POST /reconcile`` -- reconcile the tenant's pending requests in
231	  resumable batches by calling the storage layer's
232	  :meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_batch`. The tenant follows the existing
233	  ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the only query parameters are ``cursor``
234	  and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100), each at most once. The endpoint
235	  takes no body: a missing ``Content-Length`` or a length of zero means
236	  there is no body; any other body answers 400. Without a cursor a new
237	  persistent batch is created; with a cursor the batch it names is
238	  resumed from its durably committed position, so a retry after an
239	  interruption continues instead of restarting and never rewrites an
240	  already committed item. On success the single-line JSON body carries
241	  exactly ``batch_id``, ``next_cursor``, ``finished`` and ``items`` in
242	  that order: ``next_cursor`` is the opaque continuation string while
243	  the sweep is incomplete and ``null`` once it is finished,
244	  ``finished`` is the matching boolean, and ``items`` lists this call's
245	  reconciled non-accepted requests in ascending acceptance order, each
246	  carrying exactly ``request_id`` and ``status``. An unknown or
247	  duplicated query parameter, a missing or empty tenant, an invalid
248	  ``limit``, a non-empty body or a malformed, unknown or cross-tenant
249	  cursor answers 400 and neither advances a batch nor changes a
250	  request; an unreadable database, corrupt persisted batch state or a
251	  failed commit answers 503 and never leaves a half-settled item.
252	* ``GET /audit-health`` -- the instantaneous, tenant-scoped audit
253	  health summary, the HTTP public read for the storage layer's
254	  read-only :meth:`RequestStore.audit_health` snapshot. The request
255	  carries no JSON business body and the tenant follows the existing
256	  ``X-Tenant-Id``/``tenant_id`` query rule; the query string accepts
257	  no parameter other than a single ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated key,
258	  an unknown parameter or a missing or empty tenant answers 400. The
259	  single-line JSON body carries exactly ``total``, ``statuses``,
260	  ``verified``, ``unverified`` and ``reasons`` in that order:
261	  ``total`` is the tenant's request count, ``statuses`` carries the
262	  four lifecycle counts (``accepted``, ``processing``, ``completed``
263	  and ``failed``) with explicit zeros and always sums to ``total``,
264	  ``verified`` and ``unverified`` are complementary and also sum to
265	  ``total``, and ``reasons`` is a list of ``{"reason", "count"}``
266	  entries -- one per distinct stable reason code, merged across the
267	  tenant's unverified requests, ordered by Unicode code point, each
268	  count a positive integer, empty when every request verifies. The
269	  whole summary is read from one consistent read-only transaction, so
270	  a concurrent submission, status advance or inspection sweep can
271	  never mix half-settled fields from two transactions; the read never
272	  creates an inspection batch, advances a cursor, writes business,
273	  audit, anchor or key records or otherwise mutates anything. A
274	  tenant that holds no requests still answers 200 with an all-zero
275	  snapshot, never a missing-request error. An unreadable database,
276	  corrupt bookkeeping or evidence or a snapshot that cannot be taken
277	  consistently answers 503 with the single ``error`` field only,
278	  never a partial snapshot, a pseudo count, a tenant, a request id, a
279	  path or SQL text.
280	
281	The observation endpoints never advance state, create an attempt or
282	write any bookkeeping; they only read persisted rows, so their answers
283	match the persisted records after a restart. They never expose a lease
284	credential, worker identity, subject, scope or any other request field.
285	Only the two reconcile endpoints may converge execution state,
286	through the storage layer's existing atomic semantics.
287	
288	Status advancement (:meth:`RequestStore.transition`), the execution
289	orchestration (:meth:`RequestStore.claim_next`,
290	:meth:`RequestStore.finish_claim`, :meth:`RequestStore.renew_lease`,
291	:meth:`RequestStore.transfer_claim`,
292	:meth:`RequestStore.migrate_execution_leases`) and the deletion receipts
293	(:meth:`RequestStore.generate_receipt`,
294	:meth:`RequestStore.verify_receipt`,
295	:meth:`RequestStore.rotate_receipt_key`) and the anchor capability
296	(:meth:`RequestStore.verify_chain`,
297	:meth:`RequestStore.rotate_anchor_key`) and the read-only batched
298	audit inspection (:meth:`RequestStore.audit_inspection` and
299	:meth:`RequestStore.audit_inspection_summary`) exist only on
300	the storage layer and are deliberately not exposed over HTTP: over HTTP
301	the service opens request acceptance, the acceptance-receipt lookup, the
302	read-only tenant-scoped listing, the six read-only observation reads,
303	the read-only audit-chain diagnosis, the read-only audit-bundle export,
304	the read-only deletion-receipt recovery, the single-request execution
305	reconciliation, the read-only
306	policy-catalog version history, the policy-catalog publication and the
307	read-only instantaneous audit-health summary
308	described above. The
309	current-status lookup (:meth:`RequestStore.get_status`), the
310	tenant-scoped listing (:meth:`RequestStore.list_requests`), the
311	execution log (:meth:`RequestStore.get_execution_log`), the tombstone
312	page read (:meth:`RequestStore.page_deletion_tombstones`), the
313	single-snapshot request evidence read
314	(:meth:`RequestStore.get_request_evidence`), the
315	read-only audit-chain diagnosis
316	(:meth:`RequestStore.diagnose_chain`), the
317	audit-bundle export
318	(:meth:`RequestStore.export_audit_bundle`), the
319	read-only deletion-receipt recovery
320	(:meth:`RequestStore.get_receipt`), the
321	single-request reconciliation
322	(:meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_execution`), the batched reconciliation
323	(:meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_batch`), the catalog version
324	history (:meth:`RequestStore.audit_policy_catalog`), the catalog
325	publication (:meth:`RequestStore.publish_policy_catalog`) and the
326	instantaneous audit-health snapshot
327	(:meth:`RequestStore.audit_health`) back their HTTP
328	endpoints but remain storage-layer methods as well.
329	
330	Success responses are a single line of JSON followed by a trailing
331	newline. Acceptance, receipt lookup, the status read and a successful
332	reconcile render exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at``
333	(in that order); the same idempotent request and every lookup return
334	byte-identical bodies. The execution-log read renders exactly
335	``request_id`` and ``attempts``. The batch reconcile renders exactly
336	``batch_id``, ``next_cursor``, ``finished`` and ``items``, each item
337	rendering exactly ``request_id`` and ``status``. The
338	listing read renders exactly ``items`` and ``next_cursor``, each item
339	rendering exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at``. The
340	evidence read renders exactly ``request_id``, ``status``,
341	``event_count``, ``chain_hash`` and ``verified``. The
342	audit-diagnosis read renders exactly ``request_id``, ``trusted`` and
343	``reasons``. The
344	audit-bundle export renders the store's verbatim single-line compact
345	bundle text with its single trailing newline. The
346	deletion-receipt read renders the store's verbatim single-line compact
347	receipt text with its single trailing newline: exactly ``tenant_id``,
348	``request_id``, ``created_at``, ``completed_at``, ``scope_digest``,
349	``attempt_digest`` and ``tag`` in that order. The
350	tombstone page read renders exactly ``request_id``, ``tombstones``,
351	``recorded_at``, ``evidence_digest`` and ``next_cursor``, each
352	tombstone rendering exactly ``adapter_id``, ``scope``, ``operation_id``,
353	``outcome``, ``proof_digest`` and ``recorded_at``. The policy-catalog
354	history read renders exactly ``versions``, each version rendering
355	exactly ``version``, ``effective_at``, ``rule_count``,
356	``exception_count`` and ``status``. The policy-catalog publication
357	renders exactly ``version`` and ``effective_at``. The audit-health
358	snapshot renders exactly ``total``, ``statuses``, ``verified``,
359	``unverified`` and ``reasons``; ``statuses`` renders exactly the four
360	lifecycle counts in fixed order and each reason renders exactly
361	``reason`` and ``count``.
362	Error responses are single-line JSON objects with exactly one key,
363	``error``, holding a stable error code:
364	
365	``invalid_request`` (400), ``unauthorized`` (401), ``forbidden``
366	(403), ``idempotency_conflict`` (409), ``policy_catalog_conflict``
367	(409), ``audit_bundle_unavailable`` (409), ``receipt_unavailable``
368	(409), ``not_found`` (404),
369	``method_not_allowed`` (405) and
370	``storage_unavailable`` (503).
371	
372	Optional token authentication and role-based access control can be
373	enabled by passing an auth configuration (see :func:`load_auth_config`)
374	to :func:`build_server` / :func:`make_handler`. Without it the service
375	keeps the unauthenticated contract described above. When enabled every
376	matched business request must present ``Authorization: Bearer <token>``
377	for a configured principal: a missing/malformed/unknown token answers
378	``401 unauthorized`` and a principal lacking the role required by the
379	endpoint, or acting on a tenant other than its own ``tenant_id``,
380	answers ``403 forbidden``. ``POST /requests`` requires
381	``request:submit`` and the target tenant is the body's ``tenant_id``;
382	each of the ten GET endpoints requires
383	``request:read`` and the target tenant follows the existing
384	``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the
385	single-request reconciliation ``POST /requests/{request_id}/reconcile``
386	requires ``request:reconcile`` and its target tenant follows the same
387	existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the
388	batch reconciliation ``POST /reconcile`` requires
389	``request:reconcile`` and its target tenant follows the same existing
390	``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the policy-catalog history
391	``GET /policy-catalog/versions`` requires ``policy:read`` and its
392	target tenant follows the same existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule;
393	the policy-catalog publication ``POST /policy-catalog/versions``
394	requires ``policy:write`` and its target tenant is the body's
395	``tenant_id``.
396	The configuration keeps accepting the ``request:submit``,
397	``request:read`` and ``request:reconcile`` roles alone: a principal
398	without ``policy:read`` or ``policy:write`` simply cannot use the
399	catalog endpoints, and an
400	existing configuration without them never fails to load. Authentication runs after
401	path/method routing (unknown paths stay 404, unsupported methods stay
402	405) but before payload validation and any storage access.
403	Tokens, roles and the configuration never enter a response, a raised
404	exception message, a log record, the database or any stored artifact.
405	
406	No subject, scope, idempotency key, lease credential, worker identity,
407	database error text, SQL statement or filesystem path is ever placed in
408	a response, a log record or a raised exception message.

640	class AuthConfig:
641	    """Parsed, immutable bearer-token principals for RBAC.
642	
643	    Principals map a non-empty bearer token to their tenant id and a set
644	    of roles. Tokens and roles are kept in process memory only and are
645	    never logged or persisted by this module.
646	    """
647	
648	    def __init__(self, principals: list[dict]):
649	        # ``principals`` has already passed :func:`load_auth_config`; copy
650	        # into an immutable token -> (tenant_id, frozenset(roles)) map.
651	        by_token: dict[str, tuple[str, frozenset[str]]] = {}
652	        for principal in principals:
653	            by_token[principal["token"]] = (
654	                principal["tenant_id"],
655	                frozenset(principal["roles"]),
656	            )
657	        self._by_token = by_token
658	
659	    def authenticate(self, token: str) -> tuple[str, frozenset[str]] | None:
660	        """Return ``(tenant_id, roles)`` for *token*, or ``None`` if unknown."""
661	        return self._by_token.get(token)
662

664	def load_auth_config(path: str) -> AuthConfig:
665	    """Read and validate the auth configuration file once, at startup.
666	
667	    The file must be a UTF-8 JSON object with a ``principals`` array;
668	    each principal is an object carrying non-empty ``token`` and
669	    ``tenant_id`` strings plus a non-empty ``roles`` array of distinct
670	    values drawn from ``request:submit``, ``request:read``,
671	    ``request:reconcile``, ``policy:read`` and ``policy:write``. Tokens
672	    must be unique across principals. Any
673	    deviation -- including an unreadable or non-UTF-8 file, malformed
674	    JSON, a missing ``principals`` key or a principal missing/typing-wrong
675	    one of the required keys -- raises :class:`AuthConfigError` so the
676	    caller can refuse to bind.
677	    """
678	    # Suppress exception chaining ("from None"): the underlying OSError
679	    # carries the filesystem path and a decode/JSON error may quote file
680	    # content, neither of which may reach a raised exception message.
681	    try:
682	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
683	            raw = handle.read()
684	    except OSError:
685	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid") from None
686	    try:
687	        parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
688	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
689	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid") from None
690	
691	    principals = _validate_auth_config(parsed)
692	    return AuthConfig(principals)
693	
694	
695	def _validate_auth_config(parsed: object) -> list[dict]:
696	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict) or "principals" not in parsed:
697	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
698	    raw_principals = parsed["principals"]
699	    if not isinstance(raw_principals, list):
700	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
701	
702	    principals: list[dict] = []
703	    seen_tokens: set[str] = set()
704	    for entry in raw_principals:
705	        # Only the three specified keys are validated; their presence,
706	        # types and value domains are mandatory.
707	        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or not {
708	            "token",
709	            "tenant_id",
710	            "roles",
711	        } <= set(entry):
712	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
713	        token = entry["token"]
714	        tenant_id = entry["tenant_id"]
715	        roles = entry["roles"]
716	        if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
717	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
718	        if not isinstance(tenant_id, str) or not tenant_id:
719	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
720	        if not isinstance(roles, list) or not roles:
721	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
722	        if not all(isinstance(role, str) for role in roles):
723	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
724	        if len(set(roles)) != len(roles) or not set(roles) <= _ALLOWED_ROLES:
725	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
726	        if token in seen_tokens:
727	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
728	        seen_tokens.add(token)
729	        principals.append(
730	            {"token": token, "tenant_id": tenant_id, "roles": roles}
731	        )
732	    return principals

735	class DeferredRequestStore:
736	    """Lazily (re)initialising :class:`RequestStore` wrapper.
737	
738	    Opening the store and creating the required tables is attempted once
739	    at construction (service startup); if the database cannot be created
740	    -- an unwritable path, a corrupt file, an I/O error -- startup still
741	    succeeds and every business call retries initialization, failing the
742	    single request with the stable ``storage_unavailable`` outcome. This
743	    keeps "database cannot be created" indistinguishable from "database
744	    became unusable": both answer HTTP 503 instead of taking the whole
745	    service down, and a storage path repaired at runtime heals on the
746	    next request without a restart.
747	    """
748	
749	    def __init__(self, db_path: str):
750	        self._db_path = db_path
751	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
752	        self._store: RequestStore | None = None
753	        try:
754	            self._store = RequestStore(db_path)
755	        except (OSError, sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError):
756	            _log.warning("storage unavailable at startup")
757	
758	    def _ready(self) -> RequestStore:
759	        if self._store is not None:
760	            return self._store
761	        with self._lock:
762	            if self._store is None:
763	                try:
764	                    self._store = RequestStore(self._db_path)
765	                except (OSError, sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError):
766	                    raise _StorageUnavailable
767	            return self._store

"""HTTP layer for deletion-request acceptance, lookup, observation and
single-request and batched reconciliation.

The service exposes fifteen business endpoints:

* ``POST /requests`` -- accept a deletion request for a tenant. The JSON
  body must carry non-empty ``tenant_id``, ``subject_id`` and
  ``idempotency_key`` strings plus a non-empty ``scopes`` array of
  distinct non-empty strings.
* ``GET /requests`` -- the tenant-scoped, paginated listing of accepted
  requests. The tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule;
  the optional ``status`` (comma-separated distinct lifecycle statuses),
  ``created_from`` (inclusive) and ``created_to`` (exclusive) RFC3339 UTC
  bounds, ``cursor`` and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100) query
  parameters filter and page the result. The single-line JSON body
  carries exactly ``items`` and ``next_cursor``; each item carries
  exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` in ascending
  acceptance order, and ``next_cursor`` is the opaque continuation value
  or ``null`` at the end of the listing. Any other query parameter, a
  duplicated ``status`` value or a malformed filter answers 400.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}`` -- return the accepted request's
  receipt, scoped to the tenant identified by the ``X-Tenant-Id`` header
  (or a ``tenant_id`` query parameter). The receipt is the record frozen
  at acceptance time and always reports ``accepted``; it never changes
  when the request's status subsequently advances.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/status`` -- read-only observation of the
  request's current state. The single-line JSON body carries exactly
  ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` in that order; ``status``
  is the latest persisted state while ``created_at`` stays the original
  acceptance time.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/execution-log`` -- read-only observation
  of the request's execution attempts. The single-line JSON body carries
  exactly ``request_id`` and ``attempts``; attempts are ordered by
  ``attempt_number`` starting at 1 and each entry carries exactly
  ``attempt_number``, ``claimed_at``, ``lease_expires_at``, ``result``
  and ``completed_at``. An unfinished attempt has ``null`` ``result`` and
  ``completed_at``; a finished attempt carries its stored ``completed``
  or ``failed`` result and completion time.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/tombstones`` -- read-only, paginated
  publication of the tenant's deletion proofs for one request. The
  tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the only
  query parameters are ``cursor`` and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100).
  The single-line JSON body carries exactly ``request_id``,
  ``tombstones``, ``recorded_at``, ``evidence_digest`` and
  ``next_cursor`` in that order. ``tombstones`` holds only this page's
  entries in ascending normalized-scope Unicode code point order then
  ascending ``adapter_id``; each entry carries exactly ``adapter_id``,
  ``scope``, ``operation_id``, ``outcome`` (``deleted`` or ``absent``),
  ``proof_digest`` (64 lowercase hex characters) and ``recorded_at``.
  The top-level ``recorded_at`` and ``evidence_digest`` always describe
  the whole ledger (both ``null`` when it is empty), never just the
  page; ``next_cursor`` resumes strictly after this page's last entry
  while the ledger holds a following item and is ``null`` at the end.
  An unknown or duplicated query parameter, an invalid ``limit`` or an
  empty, malformed, foreign or stale ``cursor`` answers 400; an
  invalid, unknown or cross-tenant request id answers 404; a storage
  fault or a corrupt ledger answers 503 and never a partial page or a
  pseudo digest. The read never advances state, never creates an
  attempt or a tombstone and never changes the audit chain.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/evidence`` -- read-only request-level
  integrity verdict. The tenant follows the existing
  ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule and the endpoint requires the
  ``request:read`` role. The single-line JSON body carries exactly
  ``request_id``, ``status``, ``event_count``, ``chain_hash`` and
  ``verified`` in that order: ``status`` and ``event_count`` are the
  current status and state-event count from the same database snapshot,
  ``chain_hash`` is that snapshot's persisted 64-character lowercase
  hexadecimal chain head (``null`` when the persisted value is not legal
  SHA-256 text), and ``verified`` is true only when the events are
  replayed event by event from that same snapshot -- every link
  recomputes to its stored hash from the genesis predecessor, sequences
  run gap-free from zero, the final event's status equals the current
  status and the final link equals the head bound to the request row.
  All five fields come from one committed snapshot, so a status advance
  or a concurrent write can never mix two transactions in one response.
  When the request row, events and head are readable, a deleted,
  altered, inserted, reordered or cross-request/cross-tenant rebound
  event -- or a head that is not legal SHA-256 text -- still answers 200
  with ``verified`` false (and a malformed head renders ``chain_hash``
  null); it is never a storage fault. A malformed, unknown or
  cross-tenant request id answers 404; a missing or invalid tenant
  answers 400; an unreadable database or a snapshot that cannot be read
  completely answers 503. The read never creates or changes a request,
  a state event, an execution attempt, a tombstone, a receipt, a policy
  catalog or an audit anchor.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/audit-diagnosis`` -- read-only diagnosis
  of the request's persisted audit chain, the reason-carrying companion
  of the evidence verdict. The tenant follows the existing
  ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule and the endpoint requires the
  ``request:read`` role; the query string accepts no parameter other
  than ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated key, an unknown parameter or a
  missing or invalid tenant answers 400. The single-line JSON body
  carries exactly ``request_id``, ``trusted`` and ``reasons`` in that
  order: ``request_id`` is the normalized lowercase UUID, ``reasons``
  is the deduplicated list of stable, detail-free reason codes from
  :meth:`RequestStore.diagnose_chain` for the current database
  snapshot, sorted by Unicode code point, and ``trusted`` is true only
  when ``reasons`` is empty. An unanchored chain, a failed anchor
  authentication, an anchor head mismatch, a deleted, altered,
  inserted, reordered or cross-request/cross-tenant substituted event
  still answers 200 with non-empty ``reasons`` -- a diagnosable
  integrity problem is never a read failure. Repeated reads of the same
  persisted chain without new writes return byte-identical bodies, and
  no subject, raw scope, idempotency key, execution credential, anchor
  secret, SQL text or filesystem path is ever exposed. A malformed,
  unknown or cross-tenant request id answers 404; an unreadable
  database, an incomplete snapshot or a corrupt persisted record
  answers 503. The read never repairs, backfills, recomputes or
  overwrites anything: it never creates or changes a request, a state
  event, an execution attempt, a tombstone, a receipt, an audit anchor
  or a key generation, and it never writes an audit event or creates a
  batch.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/audit-bundle`` -- read-only export of
  the request's settled audit chain as a portable evidence bundle. The
  tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule and the
  endpoint requires the ``request:read`` role; the query string accepts
  no parameter other than ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated key, an unknown
  parameter or a missing or conflicting tenant answers 400. The body is
  the verbatim single-line compact UTF-8 JSON text (with its single
  trailing newline) produced by
  :meth:`RequestStore.export_audit_bundle` from the same database
  snapshot -- never wrapped in a response object, re-ordered, indented
  or summarised. Repeated reads at the same chain head return
  byte-identical bodies; status events appended afterwards produce a
  new bundle but never change a previously rendered text, and no other
  request's events, a subject, a raw scope, an idempotency key, a claim
  credential or any anchor secret is ever exposed. A malformed, unknown
  or cross-tenant request id answers 404 with one detail-free outcome;
  a request whose audit chain has not settled, whose historical anchor
  secret is missing or whose evidence is untrusted answers 409 with
  exactly ``audit_bundle_unavailable`` and never a partial text; an
  unreadable database, a failed snapshot read or corrupt evidence
  answers 503. The read never modifies persisted evidence, never
  writes an audit event and never creates a batch.
  The export also honours HTTP conditional reads: every 200 response
  carries a strong ``ETag`` of the form ``"sha256:<64 lowercase hex>"``
  computed over the exact body bytes, so the same body always yields
  the same tag -- across repeat reads, concurrent readers and process
  restarts -- and any body change yields a different tag. A request
  may send one ``If-None-Match`` header holding a comma-separated list
  of entity tags; when any whitespace-stripped double-quoted tag is
  exactly equal to the current tag, or a tag is ``*`` and the bundle
  is exportable, the answer is ``304`` with no body, a zero
  ``Content-Length`` and the same ``ETag`` instead of the full 200
  body. Non-matching tags, lists where no tag matches and weak
  ``W/``-prefixed tags all receive the full 200 body. More than one
  ``If-None-Match`` header, an empty field value, a control character
  or a value that is neither a legal double-quoted entity tag nor
  ``*`` answers 400 with exactly ``invalid_request`` after
  authentication, tenant and query validation but before any storage
  access. The 404/409/503 outcomes above still take precedence over
  the conditional evaluation: the tag is only compared once the
  bundle has been exported, and the conditional read never writes to
  the database, generates an event or changes the exported bytes.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/deletion-receipt`` -- read-only
  publication of the request's already-settled deletion execution
  receipt, so a caller recovers the frozen receipt without ever
  touching a signature key. The tenant follows the existing
  ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule and the endpoint requires the
  ``request:read`` role; the query string accepts no parameter other
  than ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated key, an unknown parameter or a
  missing or empty tenant answers 400. The body is the verbatim
  single-line compact UTF-8 JSON text (with its single trailing
  newline) returned by :meth:`RequestStore.get_receipt` for the same
  tenant and request -- exactly ``tenant_id``, ``request_id``,
  ``created_at``, ``completed_at``, ``scope_digest``,
  ``attempt_digest`` and ``tag`` in that fixed order, never wrapped,
  re-ordered, indented or recomputed. Repeated reads, reads across a
  process rebuild, concurrent reads and reads before and after a
  receipt key rotation all return byte-identical bodies, and no
  subject, raw scope, idempotency key, signature key, key fingerprint
  or execution credential is ever exposed. A malformed, unknown or
  cross-tenant request id answers 404 with one detail-free outcome; a
  request that exists but has no settled first receipt answers 409
  with exactly ``receipt_unavailable``; an unreadable database, a
  corrupt persisted receipt or an inconsistent snapshot answers 503.
  The read never mints a receipt, never registers a key generation,
  never advances any state and never rewrites any evidence.
* ``GET /policy-catalog/versions`` -- read-only publication of the
  tenant's policy-catalog version history, without any subject detail.
  The tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the query
  string accepts no parameter other than ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated
  key, an unknown parameter or an empty or malformed tenant answers 400.
  The body is the verbatim single-line compact UTF-8 JSON text (with its
  single trailing newline) produced by
  :meth:`RequestStore.audit_policy_catalog`: exactly ``versions`` at the
  top level, versions in ascending order, each carrying exactly
  ``version``, ``effective_at``, ``rule_count``, ``exception_count`` and
  ``status`` -- never a policy id, selector, reason, subject or any raw
  catalog content. The read never creates or advances a catalog version,
  request, attempt, tombstone, receipt or audit record, so repeated
  reads and reads after a restart return the same snapshot. A tenant
  without publications answers 200 with an empty ``versions`` array; a
  corrupt catalog or any storage failure answers 503 and never a
  partial history or a fabricated summary.
* ``POST /policy-catalog/versions`` -- the single policy-catalog
  publication entry point. The JSON body must carry exactly
  ``tenant_id``, ``rules`` and ``exceptions``: the tenant is taken from
  the body alone, and the two catalogs follow the existing retention
  format -- ``rules`` maps each policy id to exactly ``selector``,
  ``days`` and ``reason`` and must hold the whole-data ``*`` default
  rule, ``exceptions`` maps each policy id to the same three plus
  ``subject``, with policy ids unique across both catalogs. The catalogs
  are normalized with the existing selector grammar, non-boolean
  non-negative day counts and non-empty reasons before storage is
  touched. On success the single-line JSON body carries exactly
  ``version`` and ``effective_at``: the first publication is version 1,
  republishing the same normalized catalog reuses the first version and
  its effective time without writing, and a different catalog is issued
  the next consecutive version. Concurrent identical publications land
  once; concurrent publications of different catalogs have a single
  winner and every losing call answers 409 with exactly
  ``policy_catalog_conflict``. A non-object body, missing or extra
  fields, an illegal catalog shape, an out-of-range value, a missing
  default rule or a duplicated policy id answers 400 and writes nothing;
  a storage fault or a failed transaction answers 503 and never leaves
  a half-written version.
* ``POST /requests/{request_id}/reconcile`` -- reconcile exactly one
  request's execution record against its persisted state by calling the
  storage layer's :meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_execution`. The endpoint
  takes no business parameters: a missing ``Content-Length`` or a length
  of zero means there is no body; any other body answers 400. On success
  it answers 200 with the same single-line JSON shape as the status
  read -- exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` --
  rendering the current record after reconciliation. Repeating the call
  never changes a stable terminal state, historical attempts or existing
  timestamps; concurrent calls leave the unique outcome to the store's
  atomic commit. No subject, scope, idempotency key, worker, lease
  credential or attempt detail is ever exposed.
* ``POST /reconcile`` -- reconcile the tenant's pending requests in
  resumable batches by calling the storage layer's
  :meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_batch`. The tenant follows the existing
  ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the only query parameters are ``cursor``
  and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100), each at most once. The endpoint
  takes no body: a missing ``Content-Length`` or a length of zero means
  there is no body; any other body answers 400. Without a cursor a new
  persistent batch is created; with a cursor the batch it names is
  resumed from its durably committed position, so a retry after an
  interruption continues instead of restarting and never rewrites an
  already committed item. On success the single-line JSON body carries
  exactly ``batch_id``, ``next_cursor``, ``finished`` and ``items`` in
  that order: ``next_cursor`` is the opaque continuation string while
  the sweep is incomplete and ``null`` once it is finished,
  ``finished`` is the matching boolean, and ``items`` lists this call's
  reconciled non-accepted requests in ascending acceptance order, each
  carrying exactly ``request_id`` and ``status``. An unknown or
  duplicated query parameter, a missing or empty tenant, an invalid
  ``limit``, a non-empty body or a malformed, unknown or cross-tenant
  cursor answers 400 and neither advances a batch nor changes a
  request; an unreadable database, corrupt persisted batch state or a
  failed commit answers 503 and never leaves a half-settled item.
* ``GET /audit-health`` -- the instantaneous, tenant-scoped audit
  health summary, the HTTP public read for the storage layer's
  read-only :meth:`RequestStore.audit_health` snapshot. The request
  carries no JSON business body and the tenant follows the existing
  ``X-Tenant-Id``/``tenant_id`` query rule; the query string accepts
  no parameter other than a single ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated key,
  an unknown parameter or a missing or empty tenant answers 400. The
  single-line JSON body carries exactly ``total``, ``statuses``,
  ``verified``, ``unverified`` and ``reasons`` in that order:
  ``total`` is the tenant's request count, ``statuses`` carries the
  four lifecycle counts (``accepted``, ``processing``, ``completed``
  and ``failed``) with explicit zeros and always sums to ``total``,
  ``verified`` and ``unverified`` are complementary and also sum to
  ``total``, and ``reasons`` is a list of ``{"reason", "count"}``
  entries -- one per distinct stable reason code, merged across the
  tenant's unverified requests, ordered by Unicode code point, each
  count a positive integer, empty when every request verifies. The
  whole summary is read from one consistent read-only transaction, so
  a concurrent submission, status advance or inspection sweep can
  never mix half-settled fields from two transactions; the read never
  creates an inspection batch, advances a cursor, writes business,
  audit, anchor or key records or otherwise mutates anything. A
  tenant that holds no requests still answers 200 with an all-zero
  snapshot, never a missing-request error. An unreadable database,
  corrupt bookkeeping or evidence or a snapshot that cannot be taken
  consistently answers 503 with the single ``error`` field only,
  never a partial snapshot, a pseudo count, a tenant, a request id, a
  path or SQL text.

The observation endpoints never advance state, create an attempt or
write any bookkeeping; they only read persisted rows, so their answers
match the persisted records after a restart. They never expose a lease
credential, worker identity, subject, scope or any other request field.
Only the two reconcile endpoints may converge execution state,
through the storage layer's existing atomic semantics.

Status advancement (:meth:`RequestStore.transition`), the execution
orchestration (:meth:`RequestStore.claim_next`,
:meth:`RequestStore.finish_claim`, :meth:`RequestStore.renew_lease`,
:meth:`RequestStore.transfer_claim`,
:meth:`RequestStore.migrate_execution_leases`) and the deletion receipts
(:meth:`RequestStore.generate_receipt`,
:meth:`RequestStore.verify_receipt`,
:meth:`RequestStore.rotate_receipt_key`) and the anchor capability
(:meth:`RequestStore.verify_chain`,
:meth:`RequestStore.rotate_anchor_key`) and the read-only batched
audit inspection (:meth:`RequestStore.audit_inspection` and
:meth:`RequestStore.audit_inspection_summary`) exist only on
the storage layer and are deliberately not exposed over HTTP: over HTTP
the service opens request acceptance, the acceptance-receipt lookup, the
read-only tenant-scoped listing, the six read-only observation reads,
the read-only audit-chain diagnosis, the read-only audit-bundle export,
the read-only deletion-receipt recovery, the single-request execution
reconciliation, the read-only
policy-catalog version history, the policy-catalog publication and the
read-only instantaneous audit-health summary
described above. The
current-status lookup (:meth:`RequestStore.get_status`), the
tenant-scoped listing (:meth:`RequestStore.list_requests`), the
execution log (:meth:`RequestStore.get_execution_log`), the tombstone
page read (:meth:`RequestStore.page_deletion_tombstones`), the
single-snapshot request evidence read
(:meth:`RequestStore.get_request_evidence`), the
read-only audit-chain diagnosis
(:meth:`RequestStore.diagnose_chain`), the
audit-bundle export
(:meth:`RequestStore.export_audit_bundle`), the
read-only deletion-receipt recovery
(:meth:`RequestStore.get_receipt`), the
single-request reconciliation
(:meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_execution`), the batched reconciliation
(:meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_batch`), the catalog version
history (:meth:`RequestStore.audit_policy_catalog`), the catalog
publication (:meth:`RequestStore.publish_policy_catalog`) and the
instantaneous audit-health snapshot
(:meth:`RequestStore.audit_health`) back their HTTP
endpoints but remain storage-layer methods as well.

Success responses are a single line of JSON followed by a trailing
newline. Acceptance, receipt lookup, the status read and a successful
reconcile render exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at``
(in that order); the same idempotent request and every lookup return
byte-identical bodies. The execution-log read renders exactly
``request_id`` and ``attempts``. The batch reconcile renders exactly
``batch_id``, ``next_cursor``, ``finished`` and ``items``, each item
rendering exactly ``request_id`` and ``status``. The
listing read renders exactly ``items`` and ``next_cursor``, each item
rendering exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at``. The
evidence read renders exactly ``request_id``, ``status``,
``event_count``, ``chain_hash`` and ``verified``. The
audit-diagnosis read renders exactly ``request_id``, ``trusted`` and
``reasons``. The
audit-bundle export renders the store's verbatim single-line compact
bundle text with its single trailing newline. The
deletion-receipt read renders the store's verbatim single-line compact
receipt text with its single trailing newline: exactly ``tenant_id``,
``request_id``, ``created_at``, ``completed_at``, ``scope_digest``,
``attempt_digest`` and ``tag`` in that order. The
tombstone page read renders exactly ``request_id``, ``tombstones``,
``recorded_at``, ``evidence_digest`` and ``next_cursor``, each
tombstone rendering exactly ``adapter_id``, ``scope``, ``operation_id``,
``outcome``, ``proof_digest`` and ``recorded_at``. The policy-catalog
history read renders exactly ``versions``, each version rendering
exactly ``version``, ``effective_at``, ``rule_count``,
``exception_count`` and ``status``. The policy-catalog publication
renders exactly ``version`` and ``effective_at``. The audit-health
snapshot renders exactly ``total``, ``statuses``, ``verified``,
``unverified`` and ``reasons``; ``statuses`` renders exactly the four
lifecycle counts in fixed order and each reason renders exactly
``reason`` and ``count``.
Error responses are single-line JSON objects with exactly one key,
``error``, holding a stable error code:

``invalid_request`` (400), ``unauthorized`` (401), ``forbidden``
(403), ``idempotency_conflict`` (409), ``policy_catalog_conflict``
(409), ``audit_bundle_unavailable`` (409), ``receipt_unavailable``
(409), ``not_found`` (404),
``method_not_allowed`` (405) and
``storage_unavailable`` (503).

Optional token authentication and role-based access control can be
enabled by passing an auth configuration (see :func:`load_auth_config`)
to :func:`build_server` / :func:`make_handler`. Without it the service
keeps the unauthenticated contract described above. When enabled every
matched business request must present ``Authorization: Bearer <token>``
for a configured principal: a missing/malformed/unknown token answers
``401 unauthorized`` and a principal lacking the role required by the
endpoint, or acting on a tenant other than its own ``tenant_id``,
answers ``403 forbidden``. ``POST /requests`` requires
``request:submit`` and the target tenant is the body's ``tenant_id``;
each of the ten GET endpoints requires
``request:read`` and the target tenant follows the existing
``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the
single-request reconciliation ``POST /requests/{request_id}/reconcile``
requires ``request:reconcile`` and its target tenant follows the same
existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the
batch reconciliation ``POST /reconcile`` requires
``request:reconcile`` and its target tenant follows the same existing
``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the policy-catalog history
``GET /policy-catalog/versions`` requires ``policy:read`` and its
target tenant follows the same existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule;
the policy-catalog publication ``POST /policy-catalog/versions``
requires ``policy:write`` and its target tenant is the body's
``tenant_id``.
The configuration keeps accepting the ``request:submit``,
``request:read`` and ``request:reconcile`` roles alone: a principal
without ``policy:read`` or ``policy:write`` simply cannot use the
catalog endpoints, and an
existing configuration without them never fails to load. Authentication runs after
path/method routing (unknown paths stay 404, unsupported methods stay
405) but before payload validation and any storage access.
Tokens, roles and the configuration never enter a response, a raised
exception message, a log record, the database or any stored artifact.

No subject, scope, idempotency key, lease credential, worker identity,
database error text, SQL statement or filesystem path is ever placed in
a response, a log record or a raised exception message.

import json
import logging
import re
